title: Vishal Bhardwaj Just Got an Oscar Vote — and Five More Indians Walked In With Him
excerpt: The Academy's 2026 class is its most Indian yet: from the man who made Shakespeare bleed in Mumbai to the editor who cut RRR, six film professionals now decide who gets the gold
body:
There's a particular kind of power that comes without a trophy. No stage, no envelope, no tearful acceptance speech. Just a quiet invitation that says: *you now decide who gets one.*

**Vishal Bhardwaj** — the filmmaker and composer who turned Shakespeare's blood-soaked tragedies into some of the finest Hindi films ever made — has been invited to join the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences as part of its 2026 membership class. The man behind *Maqbool*, *Omkara*, and *Haider* can now vote for the Oscars. Let that sink in for a moment.

But Bhardwaj didn't walk in alone. Five other Indian film professionals received invitations alongside him, making this the most significant Indian intake the Academy has seen in years. Together, they represent the kind of behind-the-screen talent that rarely makes headlines but shapes every frame you remember.

## The Indians in the Room

**A. Sreekar Prasad**, arguably the most decorated film editor in Indian cinema history, received his invitation in the Film Editing branch. With a career spanning 45 years and more than 600 films across 17 languages — including *RRR*, *Dil Chahta Hai*, and *Saathiya* — Prasad is the kind of craftsman whose scissors have touched more of Indian cinema than most directors' cameras have.

**Deepa Bhatia**, also invited in Editing, is the woman who shaped the emotional rhythms of *Taare Zameen Par*, *Rock On!!*, *My Name Is Khan*, and *Kai Po Che*. If you've ever cried at an Aamir Khan film — and let's be honest, you have — Bhatia's cuts had something to do with it.

**Eka Lakhani** enters through Costume Design, carrying credentials that read like a tour of recent Bollywood's most visually sumptuous films: *Ponniyin Selvan*, *Sanju*, *Shershaah*, *Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani*, and *Dunki*. She dressed Vicky Kaushal for the trenches of Kargil and Ranveer Singh for the gilded chaos of Rocky. She knows what stardom looks like in fabric.

**Dilip Shankar**, one of India's most respected casting directors, was invited to the Casting branch. His eye for talent placed real faces in *Bhaag Milkha Bhaag* and *Life of Pi*, and he was instrumental in *Last Film Show* — India's official Oscar entry in 2023 that enchanted audiences with its sun-drenched love letter to cinema itself.

Rounding out the Indian contingent is **Shalini Kantayya**, a documentary filmmaker whose work has earned recognition at Sundance and beyond, and **Avneet Kaur**, who serves as Head of Characters and Technical Animation at Walt Disney Animation Studios. Their inclusion extends Indian representation into branches that have historically been dominated by Western names.

Additional India-linked invitees include production and technology specialists **Farah Khan** and **Rajesh Ramachandran**, and visual effects professionals **Becky Graham** and **Jay Mehta** — pushing the total number of Indian and India-connected professionals in this class into double digits.

## The Numbers That Matter

The Academy's 2026 class includes 529 new invitees worldwide — among them 95 Oscar nominees, 21 winners, and a Hollywood roster that reads like a casting director's fever dream: **Jacob Elordi**, **Jenna Ortega**, **Mia Goth**, **Bill Skarsgård**, **Simu Liu**, the **Safdie brothers**, and **Stephen Fry**. Disney CEO **Josh D'Amaro** also made the cut.

Women account for 42 per cent of this year's invitees, 56 per cent belong to underrepresented communities, and 53 per cent hail from 60 countries outside the United States. If all invitees accept, the Academy's total membership will swell to 11,319 — nearly double what it was a decade ago.

> "We are delighted to invite this remarkable group of film artists and professionals from around the world to join the Academy. Through their commitment to filmmaking, this year's exceptionally talented class has made significant contributions to our global movie industry." — **Academy CEO Bill Kramer and President Lynette Howell Taylor**

## Why the Diaspora Should Care

Academy membership is not honorary. It's functional. These professionals now get to vote on Oscar nominations and winners — which means Indian sensibilities will directly influence which films the world considers the year's best. In a year when Indian cinema is producing tentpoles at the scale of *Ramayana* and *Mahavatar*, and when crossover stars like **Priyanka Chopra** and **Dev Patel** are embedded in Hollywood's A-list, having Indian voices inside the voting room is no longer symbolic. It's strategic.

Bhardwaj turned *Macbeth* into a Mumbai underworld saga and taught a generation that Indian stories could hold Shakespeare's weight without flinching. Now he'll sit among the people who decide which stories matter globally.

That's not just recognition. That's a seat at the table where the menu is written.
